summary:
The FX system is complete in src/fx (19 modules + 1 test file, replacing the stub; factory `createFxSystem(ctx)` unchanged). All gates pass: fx type-check clean, 44/44 unit tests, smoke 48/48 on port 5211.

What it is:
- **Eight instanced batches in total** (budget 25): particles alpha, particles additive, streaks (tracers + beams + glow dots), ribbons (bolts + trails), telegraphs, decals, damage numbers, weather. Seven shader programs, all compiled in init().
- **Particle core**: one fixed pool of 4000 (struct-of-arrays), two clocks, billboards / velocity-stretched / plane-aligned quads expanded in the vertex shader. Procedural 4x4 sprite atlas and a distance-field digit strip, both computed as bytes (no canvas).
- **Effect library**: an exhaustive `Record<FxId, Recipe>` with 105 layered recipes. Bursts end within 2.5 s and stream puffs within 0.25 s (enforced by a clamp and by a unit test over every id).
- **Everything else in the assignment**: tracers, one-shot and persistent beams, jagged branching bolts with re-strike, six telegraph kinds, clipped procedural decals, distance-sampled trails, merging damage numbers, the 6-light pool, weather for all five ids, and the ambient storm.

Seen working in the running game: every family was fired in front of a free camera and looked at, plus first-person runs through the stub gameplay systems and the combat system that was finished meanwhile. Looks were judged through my own scratch stand-in for the real post chain (HDR target, bloom, ACES, fog), because render is still a stub — the final look under the real renderer is not verified.

Two things fall short of the assignment: armour hits cannot get their own damage-number style (the contract has no flag for it), and billboards are softened only against the floor, not against walls.

gates.typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E "^src/fx/"` prints nothing: 0 errors in src/fx (0 errors in all of src at the time of the last run). Also clean for src/fx with --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters.
gates.unitTests: `npx vitest run src/fx`: 1 file, 44 tests, 44 passed, 0 failed. Covers pool exhaustion and priority eviction, cap lowering, both clocks, NaN / Infinity / zero / negative / huge steps, debris bounce, every FxId spawning with finite output, burst <= 2.5 s and stream <= 0.25 s for every id, hostile options, the shock ring ending exactly on the given radius, quality thinning (core count identical on low / high / ultra), handle invalidation on stop / expiry / cancelOwner / clear / reset, pool caps for beams, telegraphs and trails, the light pool, number merging, decal rules, bolt strobing vs reduce flashes, tracers, weather sync, storm rate and test-mode gating, flush only in the last substep, reset giving an identical second run, dispose, error containment. The allocation test only measures when GC is exposed; run separately with `NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc ... --pool=forks` it passed (< 600 KB heap growth over 600 heavy frames).
gates.smoke: `node tools/smoke.mjs --mode dev --port 5211`: ok = true, 48 of 48 checks passed, no failure text. Run three times; the last run was after the final code change and with the finished combat system in the tree.
gates.liveCheck: Headless Chromium, dev mode, port 5211, 960x540 (hero frames 1280x720). Looked at: contact sheets of all 105 FxIds (weapons, impacts, blasts, deaths, enemy kinds, boss, player, director, world), tracers, rail / laser / lock / sweep beams, bolts incl. the reduce-flashes variant, all six telegraph kinds, all six decal kinds fresh and aged on a light surface incl. edge clipping, all eight trails incl. a detached one, damage numbers near / far / merged / over an explosion, weather in all four times of day, a storm strike over three frames, and first-person runs (arrival telegraph, bolt, tracers, numbers, deaths, combat.explode r=5, Overclock). Measured: (1) Saturated load (4000 particles, 96 trails, 32 beams, 96 telegraphs, 160 decals, 6 lights): fx.update 0.138 ms, buffer flush 0.225 ms per frame, one explosionLarge spawn 0.024 ms, stats.batches max 8, 0 errors. (2) With the shipped stub renderer, firing every id plus all other families: shader programs 20 before and 20 after, textures 3 and 3, geometries 36 and 36 with a fixed camera; budget().fx = { visibleMeshes: 8, triangles: 16 }. (3) Storm in test mode: 0 strikes and 0 sounds in 30 s of stormnight; after fx.setWeather('staticRain') the first strike came after 8.2 s, then 44 strikes in 5 min (table: 9 per minute = 45); thunder delay 0.62 s for a strike 213 m out, played as thunderFar. (4) Quality: explosionLarge r=5 spawned 54 / 73 / 94 / 125 particles on low / medium / high / ultra with beam, telegraph, bolt and number unchanged. (5) Reduce flashes: lightFlash(2) gives 12 cd full and 6 cd reduced; a normalised 1 lights the white wall 3 m away to a mid-grey patch. (6) Steady-state heap growth of fx.update + lateUpdate in Chrome: about 110 bytes per frame over 20,000 frames, no leak after GC.

contractRequests: DamageNumberOptions has no way to mark an armour hit (only crit / shield / kill / targetId), but the ruling in brief section 8 wants armour hits dim grey and smaller. FX cannot know, so armour hits are drawn like body hits. Needs `armor?: boolean` (or `part?: HitPart`); no workaround is possible inside fx.

RENDERING CONVENTIONS tell world-space custom shaders to include `fog_fragment`. For additive layers that chunk mixes toward the fog colour and so adds the fog a second time. I include fog_pars_vertex / fog_vertex / fog_pars_fragment and apply the same fog factor myself: added light fades to zero, covering layers mix toward fogColor. The convention should say so for additive materials.

lightFlash, lightningBolt and telegraph have no clock option, so they always run on world time. The pooled light of the player's own muzzle flash therefore lasts 2.5x longer during Overclock. I followed the contract; a `clock` on lightFlash would fix it.
FX_CAPS has no decal capacity. I allocate the pool as the largest maxDecals of any preset in data/quality.ts (256 today) and treat the preset value as the live cap.
FxSpawnOptions does not say what happens when both `radius` and `scale` are passed. I made radius authoritative (scale is then ignored).

RenderSystem.warm only promises to compile shaders, not to upload buffers or textures. To avoid a first-use hitch I keep all eight batch meshes always visible with zero instances (three issues no draw call for them), so everything uploads with the first rendered frame.

There is no depth texture available to other systems, so true soft particles are impossible. I fade billboards toward the floor plane under the spawn point instead (one ctx.collision.groundHeight query per spawn).
judgementCalls: GPU buffers are written in lateUpdate() of the frame's last substep, not from onBeforeRender: three uploads attributes while building the render list, before onBeforeRender runs, so that route would lag a frame. Consequence: an effect spawned while fx is not updating (pause, perk freeze) appears on the first frame after.

Damage numbers run on ctx.time.playerDt (rise, fade and the 0.25 s merge window): they are the player's own hit feedback and should not hang during hit-stop or Overclock. The contract gives them no clock option.
The digit glyphs live in their own distance-field strip texture rather than in the sprite atlas, so fill and outline stay crisp at any size.

Light pool: fade is quadratic over `seconds`; 1 normalised unit = 6 cd; when all six are busy the weakest un-keyed flash is stolen, a newcomer weaker than everything still burning is dropped instead, and keyed slots are never stolen.
Active particle cap = 4000 x clamp(particleScale, 0.25, 1): 2000 on low, 3000 on medium, 4000 on high and ultra. Lifetimes are clamped to 2.4 s for bursts and 0.25 s for stream puffs.

'Covers exactly the radius': the shock ring's bright edge ends exactly on R (unit-tested) and the fire dome is authored to reach about R. A blast within 0.4 R of the floor is folded into a dome above it instead of half a buried sphere.
Error containment reports once per entry point (spawn, beam, ...) rather than once overall. Each subsystem's update step is contained separately; a step that throws is skipped until the next reset().
stats are live getters on the pools; stats.batches is the number of batches with instances at the last flush.

Beam `seconds` is the hold time; the visual then fades by kind (rail 0.55 s, laser 0.16 s) and handle.active turns false at the end of the hold. Persistent beams are never taken from their owner; when the pool is full a fading or one-shot beam gives way, otherwise the dead handle is returned.
Telegraphs beyond the cap recycle the oldest timed one; if all 96 are persistent the dead handle is returned. Timed telegraphs ignore setProgress.

Decal `size` is the diameter; lifetimes are 14-30 s by kind. A decal is clipped to its box face unless a coplanar surface continues beyond the edge (up to four raycasts per decal near an edge). Calls without a boxId are accepted and unclipped.

Trails sample by distance and fade by age or by length, whichever comes first, so they look the same on either clock. A jump over 60 m restarts the ribbon; a non-finite vector detaches the trail; when the pool is full only a fading trail may be replaced.

Storm strikes are placed around the centre of world.bounds, 150-400 m out and never closer than the rig's corner + 45 m. The thunder delay uses the distance to the player while a run is on, else to the rig centre. 78 % of strikes draw a bolt. Crackles play only in staticRain / vortex, gusts in any weather but clear. The test-mode gate covers all storm sounds, not only strikes.

Colour choices where the contract is silent: explosionShock and hitEnemyShield default to elite magenta; tickArm pulses hazard yellow; hazardArc uses lightning white-violet; gateDenied is a cyan ripple, no red; heal effects use the health green; Overclock, last stand, perk and weak-point hit sparks use the Overclock gold; mortar and missile trails default to magenta, rocket / grenade / supply trails to cyan. Generic fire, sparks, smoke and dust use neutral colours.

Weather tints are derived from render.lighting (sun and fog colour) so they follow the grade; static rain is a pale steel white and the vortex streaks take the eclipse sun colour, so no accent colour is spent on weather.
Enemy death, muzzle and charge effects read ENEMIES[type].accent and radius at spawn time, so they follow the elite recolour of lancer and bulwark when that row is changed.
Damage numbers are drawn with the depth test off (always readable, also through walls) and sized as a fixed world height up close and a fixed angular height far away.
Only muzzle-flash layers and wisps inherit opts.velocity fully or partly; blast flashes do not, so a blast does not drift with a projectile's velocity.
integrationNotes: Render is still a stub. All look judgements were made through my own scratch stand-in (HDR target, bloom above ~1, ACES, FogExp2). Intensities will need a look once the real post chain exists; in the stub renderer the linear shader output goes to the canvas un-encoded and clipped, which is expected.

FX reads from render: lighting.sunColor / ambientColor / fogColor (as linear THREE.Color), sunIntensity, ambientIntensity, storm and flash; qualityParams in init and on 'quality:changed'; width / height in init and 'view:resize' (CSS pixels, used for minimum pixel widths). The shaders assume a perspective camera and never write destination alpha.
scene.fog must already be set when ctx.render.warm(root) runs in fx.init(), or the seven fx programs recompile on first use (render's own rule).

The finished combat system was verified live: combat.explode spawns the blast with opts.radius and normal, adds the decal, the pooled light and 'shockwaveRing' for air bursts; projectile trails arrive with combat's accent colour; hit sparks and merged damage numbers work.

Weapons, player, enemies, director and world are still stubs: their effects were fired only through the debug API, never in their real moment, position or scale. Boss effects are authored for a 5 m radius hull, deaths for the ENEMIES table sizes.
What owners must pass: `dir` = shot travel direction for hitEnemy* (the recipe reverses it) and for muzzles; `normal` for impacts; `charge` for the charge streams; stream ids re-spawned every 0.05 s.

Persistent beams (seconds: 0) show whatever set() last gave them; the pool holds 32. Thin beams and bolts are clamped to a minimum on-screen width, but callers of distant bolts should still pass a real width (the storm uses about 1 % of the distance).
Telegraphs and ground rings are flat quads at the given height (lifted 3 cm, polygon offset -2/-2). Across a ledge the overhanging part floats or is buried.

FX calls ctx.collision.groundHeight once per spawn that has clouds, glows or bouncing debris, and ctx.collision.raycast up to four times per decal near a box edge. It reads ctx.player.position and ctx.world.bossArena.center for the vortex swirl, and ctx.world.bounds for storm strikes.

The storm calls render.lightningFlash with the full intensity (about 0.32-0.95) and a unit direction, and ctx.audio.play for thunderNear / thunderFar / lightningCrack / staticCrackle / windGust with volume, pitch, delay and priority set. Audio is a stub, so none of it was heard.
Budget: the fx root always holds 8 meshes and 6 lights; budget().fx reports 8 visible meshes; a batch without instances issues no draw call.
openIssues: The final look under the real renderer (bloom, tone map, fog, sky, real level geometry) is not verified; everything was tuned against my scratch stand-in on the gray-box world.
Armour hits cannot be styled differently in damage numbers (missing contract flag, see contractRequests).
Billboards fade softly only toward the floor under the spawn point; they are still cut hard where they meet walls, crates and terrace edges.
Alpha particles (smoke, dust, debris) are not depth-sorted among themselves.
Decals near a real ledge are clipped at the box edge; the coplanar-continuation probe only looks 6 cm beyond the edge, so a mark never wraps onto a different height.

Not measured on a real GPU or at 1080p: only CPU cost and draw counts under headless software GL. Fill rate of the large fire and smoke puffs of a 5 m blast close to the camera on an iGPU is unknown (a near-camera fade and discard are in place).

About 110 bytes per frame of transient heap growth remain in fx.update in Chrome. My code allocates no objects per frame or per spawn; I could not attribute the remainder further (likely boxed doubles in not-yet-optimised code). three itself allocates a comparator closure on every buffer upload.
Thunder, crackle and gust one-shots were verified as calls only (ids, delays, counts), not by ear.
Very large sprites seen up close (boss effects at a few metres) show the texture structure of the 256 px fire and smoke cells.
The 'bullet holes on a wall' gallery cell was framed wrongly and not redone: decals were looked at on floor-facing surfaces only, wall-facing ones are covered by the same code path but were not seen.
Not checked: touch layout, the sandboxed dist build, tools/shots.mjs and tools/campaign.mjs (not required by the assignment).
